Word Problem: Courthouse Filing Fees (March)

Problem

A regional courthouse processed three case types in March:

  • 420 civil filings at a base fee of $85 each
  • 175 family-law filings at a base fee of $120 each
  • 60 probate filings at a base fee of $210 each

Rules:

  • A 6% state surcharge is added to every filing fee.
  • Electronic filers get a $5 credit per filing, deducted from what they owe: 70% of civil, 40% of family-law, and 25% of probate filings were electronic.
  • The courthouse keeps 82% of the collected total; the remaining 18% goes to the state.
  • The $9,400 passport-services revenue is separate and excluded from filing fee collections.

Question: How much did the courthouse RETAIN from filing fees collected in March?

Step 1 — Apply the 6% surcharge to each case type's fee

Civil: $85 × 1.06 = $90.10 per filing
Family: $120 × 1.06 = $127.20 per filing
Probate: $210 × 1.06 = $222.60 per filing

Step 2 — Total surcharged fees collected per case type

Case typeFilingsFee (with surcharge)Subtotal
Civil420$90.10$37,842.00
Family-law175$127.20$22,260.00
Probate60$222.60$13,356.00
Total (before e-filing credits)$73,458.00

Step 3 — Subtract the $5 electronic-filing credit

Civil electronic filers: 70% × 420 = 294 filings → 294 × $5 = $1,470
Family electronic filers: 40% × 175 = 70 filings → 70 × $5 = $350
Probate electronic filers: 25% × 60 = 15 filings → 15 × $5 = $75
Total credits = $1,470 + $350 + $75 = $1,895

Step 4 — Net amount collected from filing fees

$73,458.00 − $1,895.00 = $71,563.00
(The $9,400 passport-desk revenue is not part of this figure.)

Step 5 — Courthouse retains 82% of the collected total

$71,563.00 × 0.82 = $58,681.66
Amount the courthouse retained from filing fees in March:
$58,682
